set.overview: Adams Peak is the northernmost summit on the Sierra Peaks list, a forested, brushy bump of 8,197 feet in the northern Sierra near Frenchman Lake. The climb is a walk on old dirt roads and a use trail through meadows, ending among trees and a twin-topped summit that holds the remains of an old sighting tower. Navigation, not technical difficulty, is the challenge, especially when the roads are buried in snow.
set.approach: Drive to Frenchman Lake from Chilcoot, then follow a dirt forest road up the Spring Creek drainage; signs along it count down the distance to the peak. Low-clearance cars usually stop partway, and an eroded, rutted stretch farther on needs more clearance. Park where your vehicle is comfortable and walk the road, which decays into a trail and then a use trail through meadows to the base of the summit bumps. Where snow covers the roads, the open north ridge is gentler than the south shoulder.
set.descent_text: Return the way you came: walk down from the twin summits along the use trail, then follow the old dirt road back to your vehicle. In snow, follow your own tracks or a compass bearing, because the roads are hard to see among the trees.
hazards: Rough, rutted forest roads that can scrape or strand a low-clearance car
Route-finding in forest on buried logging roads when snow covers the ground
Brushy summit area with two bumps close in height

review.notes: Skipped gain, distance and season. Two reports give different round-trip figures from different start points (5.75 mi/1,800 ft from a parking spot about a mile short of the peak; 8-10 mi round trip from the spillway road); no figure is for a defined trailhead, and nothing states a season window. SummitPost blocked. Hazards drawn from several reports of the same approach; no hazard was inferred.

set.overview: A long, scenic approach along the Pacific Crest Trail from Rainy Pass leads over Cutthroat and Granite Passes to the Snowy Lakes, where most parties camp. From the lakes a traverse reaches the low saddle between Golden Horn and neighbouring Tower Mountain, then mostly scree and talus climb to the base of the summit pyramid. Cairns lead around to the northwest side for a final scramble of about 20 feet: easy third class, then a single near fifth-class move on a horizontal crack below the top block.

review.notes: Only the description column was in fill; wrote a fuller overview keeping the old row's facts (PCT approach, Snowy Lakes, scree, one low-5th move). Single trip page read; Mountaineers and WTA pages returned 403, so nothing from search snippets was used. The 'many climbers carry a rope' clause is mild and rests on that one report's sling and 5th-class move; remove it if too strong.
